newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks reach another record close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks reach another record close.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

CANDLR 1.3595 LME CASH ALUM US$1575.0 +26.5
CAN 30-YR 113.75 -0.30 APR BRENT CRUDE US$20.64 +0.24
* Toronto stocks rolled higher to another record close, boosted by stronger golds and base metals. * 128.5 million shares traded worth C$1.97 billion.
Toronto stocks rolled higher in brisk turnover on Wednesday to another record close for the year, reacting to firmer gold bullion and base metal prices.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 10.64 points to 6248.86, hitting the 10th record close of 1997. It also touched a new intra-day high of 6260.73 points.
Trading was heavy at 128.5 million shares worth C$1.97 billion.
"A lot of that comes from the golds," said Dunnery Best, Midland Walwyn's director of private client investment. "All the golds, across the border, are looking stronger."

Toronto's heavyweight gold group rose more than one percent while the base metal sector rose nearly two percent. They led the strengthening nine sub-indices while another five slipped. The weaker side was led by oils, transportation and banks.
"The base metals did a good job," Best added, noting that stocks were pushed upward as underlying prices rose on declining supply.
Advancing issues outran declining ones 561 to 448 in Canada's largest equities market while another 282 traded flat.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd topped Toronto's most active issues after chief executive David Walsh said on Wednesday that he would not rule out discussions with a potential suitor for the right price.

On Monday it announced a deal with Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc to develop the huge Busang gold discovery in Indonesia. Bre-X will still own 45 percent of the deposit, while Freeport-McMoRan will take 15 percent and Indonesian interests will grab the remaining 40 percent.
Bre-X shares rose 0.70 to 21.50 on 7.7 million shares.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100))
